questions.prompt: Which description best defines an atom in Grade 8 Integrated Science?
options: The smallest particle of an element that keeps its chemical identity
A mixture of many different substances
A visible grain of soil only
A complete organism made of organs
questions.correctAnswer: The smallest particle of an element that keeps its chemical identity
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that still has the properties of that element.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound.

questions.prompt: Which substance is an element rather than a compound?
questions.correctAnswer: Oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen contains only one kind of atom, while water, sodium chloride, and carbon dioxide contain atoms of different elements joined together.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound.

questions.prompt: Two oxygen atoms joined together form an oxygen molecule. Which statement is true about that molecule?
options: It is made of atoms of the same element
It cannot exist as a gas
questions.correctAnswer: It is made of atoms of the same element
questions.explanation: A molecule can be made of atoms of the same element, such as oxygen gas made from oxygen atoms.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly shows the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.correctAnswer: O for oxygen
questions.explanation: The standard chemical symbol for oxygen is O.
questions.learningOutcome: Assign symbols to selected elements.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches an element with its chemical symbol?
questions.correctAnswer: Sodium - Na
questions.explanation: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium. Carbon is C, iron is Fe, and hydrogen is H.
questions.learningOutcome: Assign symbols to selected elements.

questions.prompt: Which word equation represents the formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen?
questions.correctAnswer: hydrogen + oxygen -> water
questions.explanation: Hydrogen reacts with oxygen to form water, so the reactants are hydrogen and oxygen and the product is water.
questions.learningOutcome: Write word equations to represent reactions of selected elements to form compounds.

questions.prompt: Iron reacts with sulfur to form iron sulfide. Which word equation is correctly written?
questions.correctAnswer: iron + sulfur -> iron sulfide
questions.explanation: The reactants are iron and sulfur, and the compound formed is iron sulfide.
questions.learningOutcome: Write word equations to represent reactions of selected elements to form compounds.

questions.prompt: Why are chemical symbols useful when representing elements?
options: They give short standard names that scientists can use clearly
They make every element a liquid
They remove the need for safety rules
They show the price of each element in shops
questions.correctAnswer: They give short standard names that scientists can use clearly
questions.explanation: Chemical symbols are standard abbreviations that make scientific communication shorter and clearer.
questions.learningOutcome: Assign symbols to selected elements.

questions.prompt: A learner says carbon dioxide is an element because it is a gas. Which response best corrects the learner?
options: Carbon dioxide is a compound because it contains carbon and oxygen atoms joined together
Carbon dioxide is an element because all gases are elements
Carbon dioxide is a mixture because it has a colour
Carbon dioxide is an atom because it can be breathed out
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide is a compound because it contains carbon and oxygen atoms joined together
questions.explanation: A compound contains two or more different elements chemically combined, and carbon dioxide contains carbon and oxygen.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound.

questions.prompt: Which classroom model would best show the difference between an element and a compound?
options: Use one colour of beads for an element and two joined colours for a compound
Put all beads in a closed box without labels
Draw only the school compound fence
Use a thermometer to measure bead temperature only
questions.correctAnswer: Use one colour of beads for an element and two joined colours for a compound
questions.explanation: A model with one type of bead can represent one element, while joined different beads can represent a compound.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between an atom, an element, a molecule and a compound.

questions.prompt: Which common element is needed by most living things for respiration?
questions.correctAnswer: Oxygen
questions.explanation: Most living cells use oxygen during aerobic respiration to release energy from food.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: Copper is often used in electric wires. Which property makes it suitable?
options: It dissolves quickly in cold water
It is a strong disinfectant gas
questions.correctAnswer: It conducts electricity well
questions.explanation: Copper is a good conductor, so it allows electric current to flow through wires with low resistance.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: Why is aluminium commonly used to make some cooking pots and sufurias?
options: It is light and conducts heat well
It is a gas at room temperature
It cannot be shaped into sheets
It is used only to make pencils
questions.correctAnswer: It is light and conducts heat well
questions.explanation: Aluminium is light, can be shaped, and conducts heat, making it useful for some cooking utensils.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: Carbon can be found in graphite, which is used in pencil cores.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Graphite is a form of carbon and is used in pencil cores because it leaves marks on paper.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: Which use is correctly matched with iron?
options: Making gates, nails, and some machine parts
Producing light in all bulbs without electricity
questions.correctAnswer: Making gates, nails, and some machine parts
questions.explanation: Iron is strong and can be used in construction materials, nails, gates, and some machines.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: A community wants a metal for roofing sheets that is light and resists corrosion better than plain iron. Which choice is most suitable among the options?
questions.correctAnswer: Aluminium
questions.explanation: Aluminium is light and forms a protective oxide layer, so it is useful where low mass and corrosion resistance matter.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the applications of common elements in the society.

questions.prompt: How are particles arranged in a solid?
options: Closely packed and vibrating about fixed positions
Very far apart and moving freely in all directions
Moving with no attraction at all
Changing into new atoms every second
questions.correctAnswer: Closely packed and vibrating about fixed positions
questions.explanation: Particles in a solid are closely packed, have strong attraction, and mainly vibrate in fixed positions.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the characteristics of particles in the three states of matter.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes particles in a gas?
options: They are far apart and move randomly
They are fixed in a regular pattern
They cannot move from place to place
They are always visible to the naked eye
questions.correctAnswer: They are far apart and move randomly
questions.explanation: Gas particles have large spaces between them and move randomly in many directions.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the characteristics of particles in the three states of matter.

questions.prompt: Why can a liquid take the shape of a cup while keeping nearly the same volume?
options: Its particles can slide past one another but remain close together
Its particles are locked in fixed positions
Its particles are changed into new elements
questions.correctAnswer: Its particles can slide past one another but remain close together
questions.explanation: Liquid particles are close together but can move around one another, so liquids flow and take the shape of a container.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the characteristics of particles in the three states of matter.

questions.prompt: What usually happens to the boiling point of water when salt is dissolved in it?
options: It becomes higher than that of pure water
It becomes exactly zero degrees Celsius
It turns the water into an element
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes higher than that of pure water
questions.explanation: A dissolved impurity such as salt generally raises the boiling point of water.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effects of impurities on boiling point and melting point of a substance.

questions.prompt: Adding an impurity to ice commonly lowers its melting point. Which example applies this idea?
options: Using salt to help melt ice on a cold surface
questions.correctAnswer: Using salt to help melt ice on a cold surface
questions.explanation: Salt lowers the melting point of ice, so ice can melt at a lower temperature than pure ice.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effects of impurities on boiling point and melting point of a substance.

questions.prompt: Which change is a physical change?
options: Cooking an egg until it hardens
questions.correctAnswer: Melting candle wax
questions.explanation: Melting changes the state of wax without forming a new substance.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between physical and chemical changes in substances.

questions.prompt: Which observation is strong evidence that a chemical change has occurred?
options: A new substance with different properties forms
A piece of paper is folded
Water is poured into a cup
A stone is crushed into smaller pieces only
questions.correctAnswer: A new substance with different properties forms
questions.explanation: Chemical changes form new substances, often with signs such as colour change, gas production, heat, light, or a new solid.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between physical and chemical changes in substances.

questions.prompt: Rusting of iron is a chemical change because a new substance is formed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Rusting forms iron oxide, which has different properties from the original iron.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between physical and chemical changes in substances.

questions.prompt: A learner tears paper, then burns another piece of paper. How should the two changes be classified?
options: Tearing is physical; burning is chemical
Tearing is chemical; burning is physical
Both are chemical because paper is involved
Both are physical because both use hands
questions.correctAnswer: Tearing is physical; burning is chemical
questions.explanation: Tearing changes size and shape only, while burning forms new substances such as ash and gases.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between physical and chemical changes in substances.

questions.prompt: A pupil heats a pure liquid and a salty sample of the same liquid. Which fair comparison should be made?
options: Record the boiling point of each sample using equal volumes and the same apparatus
Use different containers and different amounts
Guess which one boils first from its colour
questions.correctAnswer: Record the boiling point of each sample using equal volumes and the same apparatus
questions.explanation: A fair test changes only the impurity condition and measures boiling point using the same method.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effects of impurities on boiling point and melting point of a substance.

questions.prompt: Which change of state happens when wet clothes dry in the sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Evaporation
questions.explanation: Water in the clothes changes from liquid to water vapour during evaporation.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Water droplets form outside a cold soda bottle on a warm day. Which change of state explains this?
questions.correctAnswer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapour in the air cools near the cold bottle and changes into liquid droplets.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which change of state is used when making ice cubes in a freezer?
questions.correctAnswer: Freezing
questions.explanation: Freezing changes liquid water into solid ice when heat is removed.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which daily activity uses melting?
options: Butter softening on a hot chapati
questions.correctAnswer: Butter softening on a hot chapati
questions.explanation: Butter changes from a more solid state to a liquid or softer state when it gains heat.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to collect clean water from salty water using evaporation and condensation. Which method is being used?
questions.correctAnswer: Distillation
questions.explanation: Distillation uses evaporation to separate water vapour and condensation to collect liquid water.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline applications of change of state of matter in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Why should learners appreciate changes of state in everyday life?
options: They explain useful processes such as cooking, drying, cooling, and water purification
They prove that all changes are dangerous
They remove the need to measure temperature
They show that matter cannot change form
questions.correctAnswer: They explain useful processes such as cooking, drying, cooling, and water purification
questions.explanation: Understanding changes of state helps people use heat and cooling safely in homes, schools, and industries.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the applications of change of state of matter.

questions.prompt: Which three things make up the fire triangle?
questions.correctAnswer: Heat, fuel, and oxygen
questions.explanation: A fire needs heat, fuel, and oxygen. Removing one of these can help control the fire.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of the components of the fire triangle.

questions.prompt: Which action controls a small pan fire by removing oxygen?
options: Covering it carefully with a fire blanket
questions.correctAnswer: Covering it carefully with a fire blanket
questions.explanation: A fire blanket smothers a small fire by reducing the oxygen that reaches it.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: A fire involving dry paper and wood is commonly classified as which class?
questions.correctAnswer: Class A
questions.explanation: Class A fires involve ordinary solid combustibles such as wood, paper, and cloth.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: Which fire class involves flammable liquids such as petrol or kerosene?
questions.correctAnswer: Class B
questions.explanation: Class B fires involve flammable liquids, so water may spread some of these fires instead of controlling them.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: Why should water not be poured on an electrical fire?
options: Water can conduct electricity and increase shock risk
Water makes all electrical fires freeze
questions.correctAnswer: Water can conduct electricity and increase shock risk
questions.explanation: Water can conduct electricity, so it can put people at risk of electric shock near live electrical equipment.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: Which situation is a likely cause of fire at home or school?
options: Storing matches safely away from children
questions.correctAnswer: Overloading an electric socket
questions.explanation: Overloaded sockets can overheat and start a fire, while the other actions reduce fire risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify causes of fire in nature and human settings.

questions.prompt: A learner sees a small fire in a dustbin with paper only. Which first response is safest?
options: Alert an adult or teacher and use approved fire equipment if trained
Run back to class and ignore it
Add more paper to see what happens
Use petrol to make the fire visible
questions.correctAnswer: Alert an adult or teacher and use approved fire equipment if trained
questions.explanation: Fire safety starts with raising the alarm, keeping people safe, and using approved methods only when trained.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: Which plan best reduces fire risk during a school science demonstration?
options: Keep fuels away from flames, tie back loose clothing, and follow teacher instructions
Test unknown chemicals by smell near a flame
questions.correctAnswer: Keep fuels away from flames, tie back loose clothing, and follow teacher instructions
questions.explanation: Good fire safety controls fuel, heat, and exposure while keeping learners supervised.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways of controlling different classes of fires.

questions.prompt: Which danger can result from uncontrolled bush fires?
options: Destruction of habitats and loss of soil cover
Instant formation of fertile soil everywhere
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction of habitats and loss of soil cover
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled fires can destroy vegetation, kill organisms, expose soil to erosion, and pollute air.
questions.learningOutcome: Acknowledge the dangers of fires in nature.

questions.prompt: Smoke from fires can irritate the eyes and breathing system.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Smoke contains particles and gases that can harm breathing and irritate the eyes.
questions.learningOutcome: Acknowledge the dangers of fires in nature.

questions.prompt: Which choice shows a responsible attitude toward fire safety information?
options: Reading safety signs and following evacuation instructions
Hiding a fire alarm from others
questions.correctAnswer: Reading safety signs and following evacuation instructions
questions.explanation: Fire safety information helps people respond quickly and protect life and property.
questions.learningOutcome: Acknowledge the dangers of fires in nature.

questions.prompt: After a fire drill, learners identify that one exit was crowded. What improvement should they suggest?
options: Use marked routes and keep exits clear before emergencies
Lock the crowded exit to stop movement
questions.correctAnswer: Use marked routes and keep exits clear before emergencies
questions.explanation: Clear exits and marked routes help people leave safely during a fire or drill.
questions.learningOutcome: Acknowledge the dangers of fires in nature.

questions.prompt: Which cell part controls most activities of the cell?
questions.correctAnswer: Nucleus
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls many activities of the cell.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in typical animal cells observed under a light microscope?
questions.correctAnswer: Cell wall
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall outside the cell membrane, while animal cells do not have a cell wall.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of the cell membrane?
options: It controls movement of materials into and out of the cell
It makes sunlight for the cell
It replaces the nucleus in all cells
questions.correctAnswer: It controls movement of materials into and out of the cell
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and helps control what enters and leaves the cell.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which cell component contains cell sap and is usually large in mature plant cells?
questions.correctAnswer: Vacuole
questions.explanation: A large permanent vacuole in many plant cells contains cell sap and helps maintain cell firmness.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis in green plant cells?
questions.correctAnswer: Chloroplast
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: A learner observes a rectangular cell with a cell wall and chloroplasts. Which type of cell is it most likely to be?
questions.correctAnswer: Plant cell
questions.explanation: A cell wall and chloroplasts are features commonly seen in plant cells, not typical animal cells.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which part of a light microscope should be used first to bring a specimen into rough focus?
questions.correctAnswer: Coarse adjustment knob
questions.explanation: The coarse adjustment knob moves the stage or tube quickly to bring the specimen into rough focus at low power.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: Animal cells usually lack a cell wall and chloroplasts.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Typical animal cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus but not a cell wall or chloroplasts.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between plant and animal cells is most accurate?
options: Both have cytoplasm and cell membranes, but only plant cells have cell walls
questions.correctAnswer: Both have cytoplasm and cell membranes, but only plant cells have cell walls
questions.explanation: Plant and animal cells share some structures, but plant cells have extra features such as cell walls and often chloroplasts.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: A class prepares onion epidermis slides. Which step best improves the observation of cells?
options: Place a thin layer on a slide and add a suitable stain if instructed
Use a thick onion piece so light cannot pass
Hold the slide with bare fingers over a flame
Ignore the cover slip and shake the microscope
questions.correctAnswer: Place a thin layer on a slide and add a suitable stain if instructed
questions.explanation: Thin specimens let light pass through, and a stain can make cell parts easier to see.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.

questions.prompt: How is total microscope magnification calculated?
options: Eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective lens magnification
Eyepiece magnification added to slide length
Objective lens magnification divided by room temperature
Mirror size multiplied by cover slip thickness
questions.correctAnswer: Eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective lens magnification
questions.explanation: Total magnification is found by multiplying the eyepiece magnification by the objective lens magnification.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: A microscope has a 10x eyepiece and a 40x objective lens. What is the total magnification?
questions.explanation: Total magnification is 10 multiplied by 40, which equals 400x.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: A microscope uses a 10x eyepiece and a 10x objective lens. What is the total magnification?
questions.explanation: The total magnification is 10 multiplied by 10, giving 100x.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: Why is magnification important when studying cells?
options: It makes tiny cell structures visible for observation and drawing
It changes animal cells into plant cells
It removes the need to focus the microscope
questions.correctAnswer: It makes tiny cell structures visible for observation and drawing
questions.explanation: Cells and their parts are small, so magnification helps learners see and record them clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of cells in living things.

questions.prompt: If a learner changes from a 10x objective to a 40x objective with the same eyepiece, what happens to total magnification?
questions.correctAnswer: It increases
questions.explanation: A higher objective lens magnification increases total magnification when the eyepiece stays the same.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion best explains why cells are called basic units of life?
options: Living things are made of cells that carry out life processes
Cells are larger than all organisms
Cells are only found in rocks
Cells are always visible without instruments
questions.correctAnswer: Living things are made of cells that carry out life processes
questions.explanation: Cells form living things and perform processes such as nutrition, respiration, growth, and reproduction.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of cells in living things.

questions.prompt: What is diffusion?
options: Movement of particles from a region of high concentration to low concentration
Movement of water only through metal
Movement of solids uphill by heating
Changing an element into a cell
questions.correctAnswer: Movement of particles from a region of high concentration to low concentration
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the spreading of particles from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the process of diffusion and osmosis in cells.

questions.prompt: Which example best demonstrates diffusion?
options: Perfume smell spreading across a room
A magnet attracting an iron nail
questions.correctAnswer: Perfume smell spreading across a room
questions.explanation: Perfume particles move from a highly concentrated region near the source to less concentrated parts of the room.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: What is osmosis?
options: Movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane
Movement of smoke in open air only
Movement of sand through a sieve
Movement of heat through a metal rod
questions.correctAnswer: Movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a more dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the process of diffusion and osmosis in cells.

questions.prompt: A peeled potato strip becomes firm after being placed in pure water. What process mainly explains this?
questions.correctAnswer: Osmosis
questions.explanation: Water enters potato cells by osmosis, increasing firmness when the surrounding solution is more dilute.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: A plant cell loses water when placed in a very concentrated salt solution. What is the likely result?
options: The cell becomes flaccid or shrinks away from the cell wall
The cell immediately grows a new nucleus
questions.correctAnswer: The cell becomes flaccid or shrinks away from the cell wall
questions.explanation: Water moves out of the cell by osmosis when the outside solution is more concentrated.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Which material would be most useful for demonstrating osmosis in class?
options: A selectively permeable membrane or living tissue
questions.correctAnswer: A selectively permeable membrane or living tissue
questions.explanation: Osmosis requires water movement across a selectively permeable membrane, which living tissues can show.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Why is diffusion important in the lungs?
options: Oxygen moves from air sacs into the blood
Bones become harder in the lungs
Food is ground into small pieces
questions.correctAnswer: Oxygen moves from air sacs into the blood
questions.explanation: Oxygen diffuses from the air sacs, where its concentration is higher, into the blood, where it is lower.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Which process helps root hair cells take in water from the soil?
questions.correctAnswer: Osmosis
questions.explanation: Water can move from the soil into root hair cells by osmosis through cell membranes.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Diffusion can happen in gases and liquids.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Particles in gases and liquids can move and spread from high to low concentration.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the process of diffusion and osmosis in cells.

questions.prompt: Which investigation design best compares osmosis in potato strips?
options: Use equal potato strips in pure water and salt solution, then compare length or firmness
Use different potato sizes and no labels
Boil one strip and freeze the other before measuring
Place both strips in the same solution and guess
questions.correctAnswer: Use equal potato strips in pure water and salt solution, then compare length or firmness
questions.explanation: A fair comparison keeps the strips similar and changes the solution concentration to observe osmosis.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Why is osmosis important for plant support?
options: It helps plant cells stay turgid when they have enough water
It changes leaves into flowers instantly
It stops all water movement in roots
questions.correctAnswer: It helps plant cells stay turgid when they have enough water
questions.explanation: Water entering plant cells by osmosis helps them become firm, supporting soft plant parts.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Which statement shows the importance of diffusion in living things?
options: It helps move oxygen, carbon dioxide, and some dissolved substances over short distances
It turns all cells into stones
It prevents any exchange with the environment
It only happens in dead materials
questions.correctAnswer: It helps move oxygen, carbon dioxide, and some dissolved substances over short distances
questions.explanation: Diffusion helps cells exchange useful and waste substances where concentration differences exist.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: A wilted leafy vegetable becomes firmer after being placed in clean water. Which explanation is best?
options: Water enters cells by osmosis and increases turgidity
The vegetable changes into a compound
questions.correctAnswer: Water enters cells by osmosis and increases turgidity
questions.explanation: Water can move into plant cells by osmosis, making them firmer when the cells regain water.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: Which learning product would best show understanding of diffusion and osmosis?
options: A labelled table comparing direction, membrane need, and examples of both processes
A drawing of a bus stop only
A list of random chemical symbols
A poem that avoids science words
questions.correctAnswer: A labelled table comparing direction, membrane need, and examples of both processes
questions.explanation: A comparison table can clearly show similarities, differences, and living examples of diffusion and osmosis.
questions.subStrandTitle: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

questions.prompt: What is menstruation?
options: The shedding of the uterine lining when pregnancy has not occurred
The movement of air in and out of lungs
The digestion of proteins in the stomach
The release of sweat from skin only
questions.correctAnswer: The shedding of the uterine lining when pregnancy has not occurred
questions.explanation: Menstruation is part of the menstrual cycle and involves shedding the lining of the uterus through the vagina.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the menstrual cycle and its related challenges in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which event in the menstrual cycle involves release of an egg from an ovary?
questions.correctAnswer: Ovulation
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the release of an egg from an ovary during the menstrual cycle.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the menstrual cycle and its related challenges in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which is a healthy way to manage common menstrual discomfort at school?
options: Use clean menstrual materials and seek help from a trusted adult or health worker when pain is severe
Hide severe pain and avoid all help
Stop drinking water for the whole day
questions.correctAnswer: Use clean menstrual materials and seek help from a trusted adult or health worker when pain is severe
questions.explanation: Good hygiene, support, and medical advice for severe or unusual symptoms help manage menstrual challenges safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage challenges related to menstrual cycle in human beings.

questions.prompt: Where does fertilisation usually occur in human beings?
questions.correctAnswer: Oviduct or fallopian tube
questions.explanation: Fertilisation usually occurs in the oviduct when a sperm cell joins with an egg cell.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe fertilisation and implantation in human beings.

questions.prompt: What is implantation in human reproduction?
options: Attachment of the early embryo to the lining of the uterus
Release of sweat through the skin
Movement of food down the oesophagus
questions.correctAnswer: Attachment of the early embryo to the lining of the uterus
questions.explanation: Implantation occurs when the early embryo attaches to the prepared lining of the uterus.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe fertilisation and implantation in human beings.

questions.prompt: The length of the menstrual cycle can vary from one person to another.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Cycle length can vary, so unusual pain, very heavy bleeding, or worrying changes should be discussed with a trusted adult or health worker.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the menstrual cycle and its related challenges in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports menstrual hygiene during a school day?
options: Carry clean materials, change them regularly, wash hands, and dispose of used materials safely
Use one material for many days
Throw used materials in open fields
Avoid washing hands after changing materials
questions.correctAnswer: Carry clean materials, change them regularly, wash hands, and dispose of used materials safely
questions.explanation: Clean materials, handwashing, privacy, and safe disposal reduce infection risk and support dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a plan to manage challenges related to menstrual cycle in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly places key events in early human reproduction?
questions.correctAnswer: Ovulation, fertilisation, implantation
questions.explanation: An egg is released during ovulation, fertilisation may occur in the oviduct, and implantation follows in the uterus.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe fertilisation and implantation in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which symptom can be associated with some sexually transmitted infections?
options: Pain while urinating or unusual discharge
questions.correctAnswer: Pain while urinating or unusual discharge
questions.explanation: Some STIs may cause pain during urination, unusual discharge, sores, or itching, though some infections may show no symptoms.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline symptoms of STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: A person can have an STI without obvious symptoms.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Some STIs may not show clear symptoms at first, so testing and medical advice are important when there is risk or concern.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline symptoms of STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest if someone suspects an STI?
options: Seek help from a qualified health worker for testing and treatment
Use unlabelled medicine from a friend
Share personal items to test others
questions.correctAnswer: Seek help from a qualified health worker for testing and treatment
questions.explanation: Qualified health workers can test, treat, advise, and protect privacy better than guessing or self-medicating.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain prevention measures for common STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which measure helps prevent common STIs?
options: Avoid risky sexual behaviour and seek accurate health information
Share sharp objects such as needles
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid risky sexual behaviour and seek accurate health information
questions.explanation: Prevention includes responsible choices, accurate information, medical guidance, and avoiding exposure to infected body fluids.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain prevention measures for common STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: Why is stigma harmful when discussing reproductive health and STIs?
options: It can stop people from seeking help, testing, and treatment
questions.correctAnswer: It can stop people from seeking help, testing, and treatment
questions.explanation: Respectful support encourages people to get accurate information and medical care.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the need for a healthy reproductive system.

questions.prompt: Which choice supports a healthy reproductive system?
options: Good hygiene, accurate information, medical care when needed, and respectful decision-making
Using unknown substances on the body
Avoiding trusted adults and health workers
questions.correctAnswer: Good hygiene, accurate information, medical care when needed, and respectful decision-making
questions.explanation: Healthy habits, reliable guidance, and timely medical care help protect the reproductive system.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the need for a healthy reproductive system.

questions.prompt: Which symptom should be discussed with a trusted adult or health worker rather than ignored?
options: Persistent unusual genital sores or discharge
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent unusual genital sores or discharge
questions.explanation: Persistent unusual sores or discharge can signal infection and should be checked by a qualified health worker.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline symptoms of STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: A learner is asked to design a peer message on STI prevention. Which message is most appropriate?
options: Use accurate health information, avoid risky behaviour, and seek medical help early
Hide all symptoms and avoid testing
Use medicine from friends without labels
questions.correctAnswer: Use accurate health information, avoid risky behaviour, and seek medical help early
questions.explanation: A good health message is accurate, respectful, preventive, and encourages timely care.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain prevention measures for common STIs in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which is a form of energy?
questions.correctAnswer: Light
questions.explanation: Light is a form of energy. Sand, iron nails, and glass cups are materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify forms of energy in nature.

questions.prompt: Which energy source is renewable?
questions.correctAnswer: Solar energy
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable because sunlight is naturally replenished, while fossil fuels take a very long time to form.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify energy sources into renewable or non-renewable.

questions.prompt: What energy transformation happens in a torch with batteries when it is switched on?
options: Chemical energy to electrical energy to light energy
Light energy to soil energy only
Heat energy to a new element
questions.correctAnswer: Chemical energy to electrical energy to light energy
questions.explanation: Chemical energy in the battery changes to electrical energy, which the bulb or LED changes mainly into light.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate simple energy transformations in nature.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly classifies energy sources?
questions.correctAnswer: Wind - renewable; diesel - non-renewable
questions.explanation: Wind is naturally replenished, while diesel comes from petroleum, a non-renewable fossil fuel.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify energy sources into renewable or non-renewable.

questions.prompt: Which energy transformation happens when a learner rubs hands together quickly?
options: Mechanical energy changes to heat energy
Heat energy changes to chemical symbols
questions.correctAnswer: Mechanical energy changes to heat energy
questions.explanation: Movement and friction between the hands transform some mechanical energy into heat energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate simple energy transformations in nature.

questions.prompt: A school wants to reduce use of non-renewable energy for lighting. Which option best supports this goal?
options: Install solar panels where suitable and use efficient bulbs
Keep many lights on all day
Use a petrol generator for every classroom always
questions.correctAnswer: Install solar panels where suitable and use efficient bulbs
questions.explanation: Solar panels use renewable sunlight, and efficient bulbs reduce the energy needed for lighting.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify energy sources into renewable or non-renewable.

questions.prompt: Which safety measure should be followed when using electrical energy at home?
options: Avoid touching switches with wet hands
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid touching switches with wet hands
questions.explanation: Wet hands can increase the risk of electric shock, so electrical devices should be handled safely and dry.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safety measures associated with energy transformation.

questions.prompt: Which safety practice is important when using a charcoal jiko?
options: Use it in a well-ventilated place away from flammable materials
Use it in a closed bedroom
Leave children to play with it
questions.correctAnswer: Use it in a well-ventilated place away from flammable materials
questions.explanation: Good ventilation reduces harmful fumes, and keeping flammable materials away lowers fire risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safety measures associated with energy transformation.

questions.prompt: Which application uses energy transformation in day-to-day life?
options: An electric fan changing electrical energy to kinetic energy
A stone remaining still on a desk
A closed book on a shelf
Dry sand staying in a basin
questions.correctAnswer: An electric fan changing electrical energy to kinetic energy
questions.explanation: An electric fan transforms electrical energy into movement of the blades and moving air.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the applications of energy transformation in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner must design a safe home energy-saving plan. Which plan is best?
options: Use daylight when possible, switch off unused appliances, and avoid overloaded sockets
Leave lights on to remember they work
Dry wet clothes on electric sockets
Use damaged cables until they spark
questions.correctAnswer: Use daylight when possible, switch off unused appliances, and avoid overloaded sockets
questions.explanation: The plan saves energy and reduces electrical and fire risks in a practical way.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the applications of energy transformation in day-to-day life.
